Triggers.value: Physical pain in a part of the body

Maladaptive Strategies.value: I pretend it happened to someone else
constantly check body for signs of danger or injury

Threat.value: I react with alarm when someone touches me unexpectedly
Unexpected movement nearby causes me to react as if I am in danger

Negative Appraisals.value: I will never be able to feel normal emotions again
I feel ashamed of what happened to my body

issues.item: Negative Appraisals: Survival Guilt: I feel guilty for surviving when others did not
issues.explanation: 'Survival guilt' implies a trauma context involving deaths of others or a mass-casualty/survivor scenario, which is hard to reconcile with the stated index trauma of sexual assault in the absence of any supporting items about others dying. This is a trauma-type mismatch rather than a merely unusual appraisal.

issues.item: Triggers: Feeling Happy: Feeling happy or relaxed
issues.explanation: 'Feeling happy or relaxed' can function as a trigger in PTSD, but here it is weakly integrated with the rest of the profile: the other triggers are perfume/cologne and body pain, while threat is dominated by touch/startle/flashback phenomena and appraisals focus on emotional numbing and self-reliance. The positive-affect trigger is not impossible, but in this item set it lacks a clear clinical link and looks mismatched to the rest of the formulation.

issues.item: Threat: Flashbacks: Suddenly feeling or acting as if the stressful experience were actually happening again
issues.explanation: The flashback item is not inherently implausible for sexual assault PTSD, but in this profile the rest of the network is strongly organized around hypervigilance to touch/body danger and negative appraisals, with no memory items and no trigger-to-memory/threat linkage in the formulation. A full reliving-style flashback can coexist, but here it sits somewhat at odds with the otherwise body/startle-centered pattern and appears insufficiently supported by the surrounding items.

vignette: Kamran had always been a physically active person, enjoying his work as a physical therapist and finding solace in the gym. But everything changed on that fateful night two years ago when he was sexually assaulted by an acquaintance. The smell of cologne wafting through the air still brought back vivid memories of that evening, making him feel like he's reliving it all over again. The pain in his lower back, a lingering injury from the assault, served as a constant reminder of what had happened. As Kamran struggled to come to terms with what had occurred, he found himself withdrawing from intimate situations with his wife. He couldn't bear the thought of being touched or being in a situation that might trigger another flashback. "I just feel so ashamed of my body," he would say, "like it's been tainted forever." This sense of shame and self-blame only seemed to intensify when he caught a whiff of that familiar cologne or experienced physical pain in his lower back. It was as if these triggers transported him right back to the night of the assault, leaving him feeling helpless and vulnerable all over again. Kamran's negative appraisals about himself and his body began to snowball, making him increasingly jumpy and easily startled. He would flinch at unexpected movements or touch, his heart racing with anticipation. "I just can't rely on myself anymore," he'd say, convinced that he was no longer capable of protecting himself or those around him. This pervasive sense of threat only seemed to exacerbate his startle response, leaving him feeling like he was constantly walking on eggshells. In an attempt to cope with these overwhelming emotions, Kamran began to dissociate from the experience, pretending it had happened to someone else. He would avoid thinking about the assault altogether, distracting himself with work or exercise. However, this avoidance only seemed to create a sense of emotional numbing, leaving him feeling disconnected from his own body and emotions. "I'll never be able to feel normal emotions again," he'd lament, convinced that he was forever changed. As Kamran's maladaptive strategies took hold, they began to feed back into the cycle of triggers and negative appraisals. His hypervigilance for potential threats only seemed to heighten his sensitivity to certain smells or physical sensations, which in turn reinforced his feelings of shame and self-blame. It was a vicious cycle that left him feeling trapped and helpless. Despite his best efforts to manage these symptoms on his own, Kamran finally realized he needed help when he found himself avoiding intimate situations with his wife altogether. The distance between them had grown too great, and he couldn't bear the thought of losing her due to his own emotional struggles. With a deep sense of trepidation, he sought out therapy, hoping to break free from this suffocating cycle of fear and shame. As Kamran sat in the therapist's office, he couldn't help but wonder if he'd ever be able to reclaim his life, his body, and his emotions. The smell of cologne still lingered in the air, a potent reminder of what had been taken from him. But with each tentative step towards healing, he began to realize that maybe, just maybe, he could learn to live with himself again.
